controller_terminal.detail: ROW_0_INVALID:Invalid:backend transport is not TASK_COMPLETE, terminal, reaped, and bound

canary_observation.preserved_failure: The correct subject result does not retroactively become a valid completion. The backend emitted BACKEND_ERROR after rollout reopen failed, the controller rejected the row, no completion.json was written, and the remaining two routes were aborted.

sequence: The actual backend started one fresh app-server, one fresh thread, and one first-attempt turn with dispatch_count=1 and no retry, replacement, or best-of.
_wait_task_complete found exactly one rollout for the fresh thread and exactly one task_complete for the fresh turn; its final poll returned TASK_COMPLETE_OBSERVED.
The rollout contains one exact 2239-byte provider input after the matching turn_context and one correct assistant final before the matching task_complete.
The rollout also contains one app-server precontext user response_item before the matching turn_context. That precontext item has three context fragments and is not the provider input.
_reopen_rollout selected every session-wide user message response_item, producing len(inputs)=2, then required len(inputs)==1 in the coupled identity/cardinality predicate.
The cardinality predicate raised BackendError before the exact provider-input content check and before the correct final could be captured.

The backend therefore reported BACKEND_ERROR and task_complete_observed=false in its envelope even though the durable rollout had one matching task_complete. The controller correctly rejected that envelope as not TASK_COMPLETE, terminal, reaped, and bound.

fixture_contract.base_rows: One session_meta, one target task_started, zero or more precontext user messages, one target turn_context, target-turn user input rows, target-turn assistant final rows, and one target task_complete, serialized as canonical JSONL with one LF per row.

required_predecessor_successor_receipt.predecessor: Run the current candidate-v2 _reopen_rollout against current_canary_one_precontext and retain the exact typed FAIL caused by two session-wide user messages.
required_predecessor_successor_receipt.successor: Run the replacement against the same byte-identical fixture and retain PASS with one selected target-turn input, one final, one task_complete, exact output, and zero calls. Then run every fault row and retain its declared terminal result.

regression_disposition.reason: R9-REG-007 already owns the foreground start-wait-capture-reopen transaction and the preservation of terminal metadata between task completion and durable completion construction. _wait_task_complete succeeded and the durable verifier/controller layer was not reached, so R9-REG-002 polling and R9-REG-010 verifier semantics are not the primary family.
regression_disposition.simulator_action: Add the zero-call JSONL fixture matrix and its predecessor FAIL/successor PASS receipt; retain all 20 prior families and 47 prior variants unchanged, then require the new forty-eighth variant.

delete: The session-wide collection of every user message response_item as provider inputs.
The coupling len(inputs)==1 inside the session/turn/task terminal cardinality predicate.
preserve: _wait_task_complete unchanged because it selected one rollout and one matching task_complete correctly.
The controller transport admission unchanged because it correctly rejected a BACKEND_ERROR envelope.
Exact route, model provider, output, prohibited activity, terminal-LF, process reap, no-retry, no-replacement, and no-best-of checks.
Precontext response_items remain evidence but are never treated as provider input.
replacement_selector: Enumerate rollout rows with stable row indexes.
Require exactly one session_meta and bind its session identity to the fresh thread.
Require exactly one turn_context in the fresh rollout and require its turn_id, model, and effort to equal the requested turn and route.
Require exactly one task_started and one task_complete event in the fresh rollout; both must bind to the requested turn. Reject missing, duplicate, or wrong-turn extras.

Select user message response_items strictly after the matching turn_context. Require exactly one such post-context user message across the remaining rollout, require it before the matching task_complete, and require its passthrough turn_id to equal the requested turn.

Require that selected message content is exactly one input_text item whose text equals provider_input byte-for-byte. Reject zero, two, duplicate-exact, extra-nonmatching, post-terminal, or drifted post-context user messages.

Bind assistant final messages to the requested turn and to the interval after the selected provider input and before the matching task_complete. Exactly one well-formed final is the only PASS-capable cardinality; zero or multiple finals retain typed non-PASS capture outcomes.

Keep arbitrary zero, one, or two precontext user messages before the matching turn_context outside provider-input cardinality; the selector is order-bound, not metadata-only, because the observed precontext message carries the same passthrough turn_id.
